## Findings ledger
- [D3.DOC8.F4] The authors’ additional theme is the interactive historical production of official categories: state actors introduce categories, but successful adoption depends on their resonance with social categories — dim: theme_position — anchor: "state actors introduced census categories only when they resonated with previously existed social categories" — doc: em:8AX3TFK3 — reader: Rebecca Jean Emigh, Dylan Riley, and Patricia Ahmed — theme-origin: reader_addition — theme: Interactive state–society production of legal and racial categories — plan-theme-link: outside-spine — position: The article adds an empirically specified model in which state and social influences interact across time, with legal categories becoming racialized through historically changing social relations rather than being simply imposed by the state — confidence: high

sections_inspected: Abstract and opening theoretical discussion, PDF pp. 1–4
Conceptualizing the First US Census, PDF pp. 4–6
scope_outcomes.criterion: The citing text must substantively interpret or develop a position on at least one supplied engagement theme, or introduce and support a related theme, with a verbatim anchor.
scope_outcomes.basis: The inspected article explicitly discusses Weberian state-centered analysis, Marxist class analysis, state autonomy, social meaning, and the interaction of state and social influences in producing legal and racial categories.
limitations: This finding concerns the supplied coauthored article and does not isolate Riley’s individual position.
The article does not substantively address every plan-spine theme, especially estates, political capitalism, tax-farming, and patrimonialism.
The inspected source is not evidence about the thinker’s complete reception or the authors’ complete works.

evidence_state.coverage_basis: reader/reviewer report; source bytes do not establish inspection or completeness
blocking_issues: One or more declared finding references lack retained verified evidence
